threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the buses are 'on time' instead of just 'not late enough to walk.'
Caught a night bus home from Brixton and overheard a couple arguing over who was to blame for the broken heating. Classic late-night drama!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: One rainy morning, I saw a guy selling homemade soup from his window, offering bowls to drenched passersby. That's when it hit me: this place has a heart.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find a kebab shop that serves its own homemade hot sauce—so fiery, it has a warning sign. A true rite of passage!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a local when they fist-bump the guy sweeping the sidewalks at 16th and Mission, not just ignore them like tourists do.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni at Civic Center today just as someone was arguing with a dog about who's getting off first. The dog's winning, obviously.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all bars serve tapas, but many locals prefer their 'pintxos'—tiny snacks skewered with a toothpick. It's a whole different vibe.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by their bewilderment in the Mercat de la Llibertat, staring at the variety of sausages like they've just landed on another planet.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'London Fields' instead of ‘Fields’ – that’s a dead giveaway. Locals keep it short, and they never say ‘London’ twice.
Last night on the 35, a guy pulled out a ukulele and started singing a mash-up of Adele and Bob Marley. Everyone just went quiet, then joined in.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw the guy in the corner café ordering a currywurst with a side of vegan kale chips. Only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You ever notice the random techno parties in abandoned buildings? Only in Kreuzberg will you dance in a crumbling kitchen while wearing a wig and a tutu.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local when they know to avoid 16th St BART during rush hour—it's like a parade of lost tourists every time.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Yesterday, I watched a group of tourists try to convince a Muni driver to let them on after the bus was full. The driver just shook his head and pulled away.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often miss the small, local bakeries tucked away. There’s nothing like a morning xuxo from a corner shop—definitely not the same as La Rambla!

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You’ll find them scrutinizing the metro map like it's written in hieroglyphics, while locals zip past without a glance.
